topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, the lecture course, and the core learning outcomes regarding cancer etiology and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Foundations of cancer etiology and the drivers of cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce cancer as a genetic and evolutionary disease while exploring how intrinsic biological processes, environmental exposures, and epidemiology determine cancer risk.

topics.label: Infectious pathogens and cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the role of infectious agents in oncogenesis, detailing the collaborative mechanisms of EBV and malaria in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and physical mutagens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms through which chemical toxins, metabolic activation, and radiation induce direct DNA damage and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, chronic inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss non-mutagenic tumor promotion, inflammatory microenvironments, and developmental host factors that cooperate with tumor initiation.

topics.label: Methodologies for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics present the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methods used to identify carcinogens and assess their mutagenic potential.

topics.label: Conclusion and everyday risk-benefit balance
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the presentation with final summary remarks on weighing the risks and benefits of carcinogen exposure.
